query: John Muir "age of 10" OR "ten years old" OR "age of ten" family emigrated United States 1849 (domains loc.gov, archives.gov, si.edu, sierraclub.org, pacific.edu, wisconsinhistory.org)
notes: Hits: vault.sierraclub.org (Fact Sheet, Geography non-map version, Day Study Guide timeline, Chronology, German bio), sierraclub.org (Wilderness Journeys intro, French and Spanish fact sheets), pacific.edu Holt-Atherton Life Chronology. Sierra Club vault pages return a 212-byte JavaScript shell to plain HTTP, so they were read in a browser tab (discovery check only, nothing saved): Geography non-map version says 'He was 11 years old' at the 1849 emigration; Fact Sheet says he attended Dunbar schools 'Until the age of eleven' and 'In 1849, the Muir family emigrated to the United States' (no age for the move). Pacific chronology (already snapshotted for MUI-F-0048) gives 1849 departure with no age. None states age 10; the institutional sources found give age 11, which conflicts with the claim (already recorded on MUI-F-0056 vs MUI-F-0024).

query: "John Muir" "at the age of ten" "sailed away from Glasgow" (same domains)
notes: Hit of interest: sierraclub.org/john-muir-exhibit/john-muir-wilderness-journeys, Graham White's 1996 introduction to the Canongate omnibus, reproduced by Sierra Club (read in browser, discovery only). It says that at the age of ten John, with his sister Sarah and brother David, sailed away from Glasgow; it names neither the United States nor the family's move, so it does not state the claim on its own, and the same page quotes the Fountain Lake memorial slab saying he came to America 'as a lad of eleven'. Other hits were the Sierra Club pages from the first search, a Boyhood and Youth chapter, Bade's Life and Letters, and a Pacific reminiscence. Nothing staged.
